question: Why must a special power of the soul be posited in relation to effects?
premises: If no such power is accepted, the soul would improperly become part of the effect.
That would undermine the doctrine that the effect pre-exists in its cause.
Therefore a specific power of the soul must be admitted in such effects.
inference: To preserve causal coherence, the soul must possess a distinct power operative in effects.
uncertainties: The compound śeṣakāryātmataiṣṭavyānyathā is dense and interpreted in line with the argument.
plain_english: Otherwise the soul would have to be taken as becoming part of the effect, which would damage the doctrine of the pre-existent effect. Therefore, in such a case, one must admit a specific power belonging to the soul.
